extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance under the Federal Transit Laws (transit agencies), private charter operators, qualified human service organizations, attorneys, and other stakeholders participating in FTA rulemaking or enforcement
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and compliance rules for 49 CFR Part 604 (Charter Service) including definitions, applicability/exceptions, registration and notification procedures, complaint/investigation/hearing processes, remedies, appeals, and related regulatory analyses. This is a proposed-rule NPRM describing existing and proposed regulatory text and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§604.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this part is to implement 49 U.S.C. 5323(d), which protects private charter operators from unauthorized competition from recipients of Federal financial assistance under the Federal Transit Laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies entities that must comply, defines terms, explains exemption procedures, and sets out contents of a charter service agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and enumerated exceptions (§604.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements apply to recipients of Federal financial assistance under the Federal Transit Laws, except as otherwise provided in paragraphs (b) through (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated exceptions include: transporting employees and certain officials within geographic area for oversight (b); non-FTA funded activities of private charter operators that receive certain FTA assistance (c: 49 U.S.C. 5307, 5309, 5310, 5311); emergency preparedness planning and operations (d); recipients using FTA funds for program purposes under 5310 or 5311 (e); emergency response actions with special 45-day rule (f); non-urbanized area training transport outside geographic area (g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Charter Service (§604.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter service means, but does not include demand response service to individuals: (1) transportation provided by a recipient at the request of a third party for the exclusive use of a bus or van for a negotiated price (with listed characteristic features); or (2) transportation provided by a recipient to the public for events or functions that occur on an irregular basis or for a limited duration and either a premium fare is charged or the service is paid for in whole or in part by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristic features include third-party negotiated price, third party collects fares, not part of regularly scheduled service, third party determines origin/destination/scheduling; second prong includes premium fare greater than usual fixed-route fare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter service hours definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter service hours means total hours operated by buses or vans while in charter service including: (1) hours operated while carrying passengers for hire; plus (2) associated deadhead hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of other key terms (Administrator, Demand response, Exclusive, Interested party, Days, Geographic service area, Chief Counsel, FTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: All terms defined in 49 U.S.C. 5301 et seq. are used in their statutory meaning; other defined terms include Administrator, demand response, exclusive, interested party (includes States, counties, cities, Tribal Nations), days (calendar days, with last-day rule), geographic service area, Chief Counsel, FTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions control interpretation of the part (e.g., demand response excluded from charter service; 'exclusive' defined by reasonable person standard; 'days' computation rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified Human Service Organization (QHSO) exception (§604.7 & §604.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: QHSOs receiving funding under one or more of the programs in the CCAM Program Inventory are not required to register on the FTA charter service website to receive charter service from a recipient; proposed rule revises definition of QHSO to align with 'transportation-disadvantaged' under Executive Order 13330.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes to remove Appendix A listing programs and instead keep the qualifying-program list current on the FTA website; only QHSOs that do not receive funding from CCAM programs must register on FTA charter website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of private charter operators (§604.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for registration of private charter operators on the FTA charter service website (with clarifying language and removal of outdated web address).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are described as not impacting existing requirements; registration remains a procedural requirement for private charter operators where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient's notification duties to registered charter providers (§604.14 & §604.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have duties to notify registered charter providers (procedural requirements for notification to the registered charter providers and duties regarding the charter registration website).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed edits remove outdated web addresses but do not change substantive requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and content of charter service agreement (§604.4 and §604.1(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Part sets out the contents of a charter service agreement and provides that the subpart explains procedures for an exemption from this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although §604.4 is noted as unchanged, the rulemaking reiterates the agreement contents are part of the regulatory scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing, form, service, and completeness requirements (§604.25–31, §604.27, §604.29–31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing complaints, answers, replies, filing procedures, service methods, and handling of incomplete complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method of service generally personal delivery or U.S. mail; presumption of service when acknowledgment received or properly addressed envelope returned; incomplete complaints may be dismissed; filing locations include regulations.gov and DOT docket operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation standards and timelines (§604.32–33)
rubrics_metrics.description: If pleadings show reasonable basis, FTA shall investigate; investigation may include review of written submissions and informal investigation; Chief Counsel must send notice when an investigation is complete not later than 90 days after receipt of last pleading due; FTA may initiate investigations on its own and request responses within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations may include additional information requested from parties; FTA may invite good faith resolution efforts; unresolved matters can be referred to a Presiding Official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief Counsel decision, appointment of Presiding Official, and hearing order contents (§604.34)
rubrics_metrics.description: After investigation, Chief Counsel may issue a decision, appoint a PO, or dismiss the complaint; if appointing a PO, the Chief Counsel issues a hearing order listing allegations, authorities, issues, procedural rules, PO contact, and the date for the PO's recommended decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing order establishes the scope and schedule for adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions (§604.35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings handled by an FTA attorney except the PO may not be an FTA attorney; investigative/prosecutorial staff may not participate in final decision on appeal and must avoid substantive communications with Administrator on the case except as counsel or witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures impartiality and separation between investigative/prosecutorial and adjudicative/decision functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO powers and hearing procedures (§604.36–47)
rubrics_metrics.description: A PO may hold pre-hearing conferences, administer oaths, issue deposition notices, limit discovery, receive relevant evidence, regulate hearings, hold settlement conferences, rule on motions, examine witnesses, and make findings and recommended decisions; parties may appear with counsel; PO may grant limited extensions; discovery scope is within PO discretion with limits on cumulative, duplicative, or unduly burdensome requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on depositions (good cause: unavailability, perpetuation, expense prevention); public disclosure presumptively open with motions to withhold for Privacy Act, trade secrets, confidential commercial/financial information; transcript, exhibits, and motions form the exclusive record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof and burden of proof (§604.41–42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard of proof is preponderance of the evidence. The burden of proof of noncompliance with this part is on the registered charter provider; except where statute or rule provides otherwise, proponent of a motion has burden of proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of proof, record, and access (§604.43–44)
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded evidence may be offered on the record when filing an appeal; the transcript of testimony, exhibits, motions, and documents constitute the exclusive record for decision; interested persons may examine the record via regulations.gov or after payment for search/reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures completeness of administrative record for appeal and public access subject to withholding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedures and effect on appeal (§604.45)
rubrics_metrics.description: PO shall waive procedural steps if all parties agree; consent to waiver bars raising that issue on appeal; parties cannot consent to waive PO's obligation to enter a recommended decision on the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits grounds for appeal when procedures are waived by consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for recommended and final decisions (§604.46–49)
rubrics_metrics.description: PO issues recommended decision within 110 days after referral; Chief Counsel ratifies or modifies within 30 days; parties adversely affected may appeal Chief Counsel decision to Administrator within 21 days; Administrator issues final decision within 30 days after reply due date or after briefs on review are due; if Administrator reviews on own motion, Chief Counsel decision is stayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timelines for both internal and appellate administrative review; failure to appeal results in Chief Counsel decision becoming final and may waive judicial review rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies and factors for determining remedies (§604.47)
rubrics_metrics.description: If violation found, Chief Counsel may bar recipient from future FTA assistance, order withholding of a reasonable percentage of assistance, or pursue suspension/debarment. In determining remedy the Chief Counsel shall consider: (1) nature and circumstances of violation; (2) extent and gravity ('extent of deviation from regulatory requirements'); (3) revenue earned ('economic benefit') by providing charter service; (4) operating budget of recipient; (5) other matters as justice may require; and (6) whether recipient provided service described in a cease and desist order after issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief Counsel may mitigate remedy based on corrective action, with systemic preventive action given greater consideration; pattern of violations may produce larger bar; withholding may be lump sum or over period up to five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and final-agency-order rules (§604.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may seek judicial review in an appropriate U.S. District Court of a final decision and order under 5 U.S.C. 701-706 by filing petition within 60 days after final decision is effective. Decisions that are not final for judicial review include: FTA decision to dismiss a complaint (§604.29), a recommended PO decision at conclusion of hearing, or a Chief Counsel decision that became final due to no appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what constitutes a final decision for purposes of judicial review and the 60-day filing deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment, docket, and confidentiality practice
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received will be posted without change to regulations.gov; agencies review submissions and may redact or withhold certain submissions or portions thereof; submitted comments may not be available to read until agency approves them; comments should include agency name and docket number or RIN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions for submitting comments: regulations.gov portal, fax, mail, hand delivery; comment due date specified (e.g., March 10, 2025) and agency contact info provided; agencies may redact personal information as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices relocation and website maintenance (Appendix A–D removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed removal of Appendix A (Listing of Human Service Financial Assistance Programs), Appendix B (Reasons for Removal), Appendix C (Frequently Asked Questions), and Appendix D (Table of Potential Remedies), relocating supplemental information to the FTA website to keep program lists current.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Appendix A is outdated; CCAM Program Inventory will be kept current on FTA website; changes intended to be non-substantive and reduce administrative burden of charter registration for QHSOs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory analyses and applicability of Executive Orders and statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency's determinations under Executive Orders (12866, 13563, 14094, 13132, 12372, 12630, 12988, 13045, 13175, 13211, 12898), Regulatory Flexibility Act, Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, Paperwork Reduction Act, NEPA categorical exclusion, and other required analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency states proposed rule is not significant under EO 12866, no expected economic effect, not a significant energy action, not expected to have substantial federalism or tribal effects, qualifies for NEPA categorical exclusion, no change to paperwork burden hours for associated OMB control number 2132-0543.
